rooms.description: What this place is for, how a thread works, and the few rules we keep.

threads.title: Welcome to the GraviQuest Forum
threads.body:
This is where the GraviQuest community talks things through.

**How it works**

- Open a room and read any thread. No account is needed to read.
- Each thread opens with a post from the team. Sign in with your GraviQuest account to reply to it, or to any reply under it, and to like posts.
- A moderator reads member posts before they appear.

Questions about the Forum itself are welcome below.

threads.title: What GraviQuest is
threads.body:
GraviQuest is a community drawn together by the weighty questions in science and AI, with a forum to talk them through.

[How the community works](https://graviquest.com/community)

Questions about GraviQuest itself are welcome below.

rooms.name: AI in Research
rooms.description: Watch, read, then talk it through: one thread for the videos, one for the essays, one for the discussion.

threads.title: Video Discussion: Is AI reliable in research?
threads.body:
This thread is for discussing the [videos in this Topic](https://graviquest.com/topic-answer-that-looked-right.html#video).

What did you find interesting, confusing, convincing, or worth questioning? What do you think could have been done differently, or what would you like to see explored further?

Feel free to discuss anything about the videos: their ideas, storytelling, scientific content, visuals, characters, production, or anything else that caught your attention.

Share your thoughts, criticism, suggestions, or alternative interpretations. We'd love to hear what you think and how we can make future videos better together.

threads.title: Essay Discussion: Is AI reliable in research?
threads.body:
This thread is for discussing the [essays published in this Topic](https://graviquest.com/topic-answer-that-looked-right.html#essay).

Feel free to comment on anything you find interesting, challenge an argument, offer a different perspective, question a claim, discuss the annotations or sources, or point out something that could have been explained better.

If you disagree with an idea, have a different interpretation, know a source worth exploring, or think we've overlooked something, we'd love to hear about it.

The essays are a starting point for discussion, not the final word, and we update them together, through discussions.
